prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an outdoor sidewalk scene bounded on the left by a storefront wall (roughly 1.5–3 m away) that recedes into the distance on the right (10–30+ m away), with a companion standing within arm's reach (about 0.5–1.0 m) on the far left. In frames 1, 3, and 5, the companion appears as a bright white silhouette in right-facing profile holding a small food wrapper within both her own and the camera wearer's arm's reach while occluding the brick pillar behind her, whereas two distant pedestrians are faintly visible as small dark shapes 15–25 m ahead on the right in frames 3–5. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer walks forward and pans right in frame 2 (causing the companion to leave the left edge of the frame) before panning back left in frames 3–5 as the companion shifts from side-profile to turning her head slightly toward the camera wearer. The depth map makes the planar geometry of the receding building facade, recessed doorway in frame 1, and ground plane gradient clearer than in the dark, motion-blurred RGB frames. However, it is severely unreliable in frames 2 and 4, where it completely misses the foreground companion in frame 4 and flattens the entire left storefront and foreground into a uniform mid-grey plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground and background figures against the unlabelled black background of the sidewalk and storefront, detecting the nearby companion (`person`, 0.5–1.0 m away on the left) in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, and two distant pedestrians (`person`, 15–25 m ahead on the right, about 0.5–1 m apart from each other) at the right edge of frames 3, 4, and 5. The companion's mask shows her cropped by the left and bottom frame boundaries in frame 1, completely out of view in frame 2, and re-entering on the left in frames 3–5 with her right forearm extended forward holding an unlabelled wrapper within arm's reach of both herself and the camera wearer. Across frames 3 to 5, her silhouette widens as she turns her head and upper torso from facing forward-right to angled slightly toward the camera wearer, while a second food item held near the bottom edge in frame 4 is partially merged into her lower mask. The map makes it easier to spot the tiny, low-contrast distant pedestrians down the sidewalk in frames 3–5 than in the dim RGB image. However, it is unreliable where it misses the companion during motion blur in frame 2, fails to segment the handheld food items as separate objects, misclassifies the overhead storefront sign in frame 3 as a `clock`, and hallucinates a tiny `person` fragment on the left window frame in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is entirely blank across frames 1–4 and detects only a single yellow upper-body skeleton in frame 5 for the companion standing about 0.6–0.8 m to the left of the camera wearer, while the storefront, objects, and distant pedestrians 15–25 m ahead remain completely unrepresented. In frame 5, the torso trapezoid and right arm keypoints place her shoulder, elbow, and wrist below her clustered facial keypoints, confirming her body is angled to the right and slightly toward the camera wearer with her lower body cropped out below the bottom edge of the frame. Although her raised hands and the camera wearer's lower-foreground hand are within arm's reach (under 0.8 m) in frames 3–5 of the RGB strip, no magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame. When present in frame 5, the skeleton clarifies the orientation of her dark-clothed torso and right upper arm against the dark brick wall and window, which blend together in the RGB image. Overall, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence, failing completely under motion blur and side-profile occlusion in frames 1–4, omitting all hand keypoints, and misplacing her left wrist keypoint near her hip rather than on her raised forearm in frame 5.
